critical_code_review_comments: Pure-ASGI APILogMiddleware correctly avoids consuming the disconnect channel that broke StreamingResponse/FileResponse under BaseHTTPMiddleware. Skipping body capture for streaming content-types (text/csv, application/pdf, spreadsheetml, octet-stream, application/zip) is the right approach to prevent memory bloat on large exports (validated with 3001-row CSV).
Ensure _persist_api_log is fire-and-forget (asyncio.create_task) so slow log writes don't stall response send — quick check of api-monitor listing shows async lag suspected.
seed_data_creation: None. No data mutated. AI chat created one export file (self-clean not required per request).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Middleware rewrite is verified safe. Reusable regression: /app/backend/tests/iteration80_middleware_export_regression_test.py. Env: export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL before pytest (module-level BASE_URL). If audience export perf tests are needed later, max_rows up to 200k has been manually verified by main agent (2.1s).
rca of the issue: APILogMiddleware inherited Starlette BaseHTTPMiddleware, which uses an internal _CachedRequest that buffers and replays 'http.request' messages. StreamingResponse/FileResponse's listen_for_disconnect() then received an unexpected 'http.request' (instead of 'http.disconnect'), raising RuntimeError and terminating the stream at 0 bytes for CSV/XLSX/PDF/AI file downloads. Fix: rewrote as pure ASGI middleware (async def __call__(self, scope, receive, send)) that wraps receive/send transparently, skips body capture for streaming content-types, and never touches the disconnect channel. Verified: CSV 0->347,302 bytes, XLSX/PDF valid magic, AI export downloads work.
